# Contributing to the GUI

In this section, contributing to the GUI is explained. In particular, adding new pages to the pipeline and adding subpages to the analysis section are described.

## Existing File Structure

The structure of the GUI is as follows:

In the main directory of the project, the file `modapp.R` can be found. This is the main app file containing the app structure, non-pipeline tabs, and navigation logic.

The folder `R` contains the files holding modules corresponding to pipeline steps, analysis step subpages, and several helper functions.

Additionally, the GUI imports functionality from the `MeDUSA/R` folder for pipeline steps. As a result, these functions can be called directly within the GUI files.

### Within Modules

Each GUI module/file in this project is divided into a UI section and a Server section.

The UI section contains code to structure the layout of the corresponding page, the Server section contains the logic for navigation and functionality of the UI components.

## Creating a New Page in the Pipeline

To create a new page within the pipeline, the template found in `New_gui_page_template.R` within the `R` folder can be used.

First, copy this file and rename it, and make sure it is placed within the `R` folder. Then rename the `new_page_ui` function at the top of the file and the `new_page_server` function within the Server section to a relevant name. Functionality can then be added or removed from the template to create the desired page.

Tip: Use `ns` and `session$ns` inside the UI and Server sections respectively to avoid naming issues caused by modularity.

Once the module page is finished, or at minimum the UI and Server functions have been renamed, the following five additions to the main app file: `modapp.R` have to be made to make the new page visible within the application.

### 1. Add UI element

Add the following line in the correct spot (matching the pipeline order) in the list found in the `Pipeline` `tabPanel` in the UI section of the main app file:

```r
div(id = "new_page_div", new_page_ui("new_page"), style = "display: none;"),
```

Replace `"new_page"` with the previously chosen name in all three occurrences.

### 2. Update page vectors

Add the chosen:

```r
"new_page"
```

to the `post_processing_pages` or `analysis_pages` vector in the Server section of the main file, depending on whether this page is before or after the analysis page in the pipeline.

### 3. Add Server logic

Add the following line in the correct spot in the Server section of the file named "Server calls":

```r
new <- new_page_server("new_page", previous_result = previous$result)
```

Ensure that naming matches the naming chosen earlier. Update the page inputs by renaming `"previous$result"` to for example `"subtraction$result"` if the page follows after the subtraction page in the pipeline. Also change the `"previous_result"` parameter for the page that used to come before e.g subtraction to keep the pipeline linear.

### 4. Add to modules list

Add:

```r
new_page = new,
```

to the list of modules in the Server section in the correct order.

### 5. Add navigation button

Add:

```r
actionButton("nav_new", "4. Button Text", class = "btn-sm btn-secondary"),
```

to the list of action buttons near the bottom of the main app file in the correct spot.

Add to the first list of the two, if it is part of the pre-processing section of the pipeline and add to the second list of the two, if it is part of the analysis section.

## Adding a Subpage to the Analysis Section

To add a subpage to the analysis section, accessible by card from the analysis hub, the same template from `New_gui_page_template.R` can be used.

In the same way as before, copy and rename the file and rename the UI and Server functions to an appropriate name. After that, the page can be modified freely.

To make the page visible the following steps have to be followed:

### 1. Add Server logic

In `8_analysis_GUI.R`, add:

```r
new_result <- new_page_server("new", analysis_data)
```

to the list of similar lines in the Server section of this file, with "new" replaced for the chosen name for the UI and Server functions within the module.

### 2. Add a clickable card

Add the following code block below the similar code blocks to create a clickable card for the new sub-page. Some adjustment to layout settings may be needed to make it fit on the page:

```r
div(
  class = "card-item",
  div(
    class = "card-box",
    onclick = sprintf("Shiny.setInputValue('%s', Math.random())", session$ns("go_new")),
    h3("New Page"),
    p("Description of the new analysis module")
  )
),
```

Remember to replace "new" for the chosen name here as well.

### 3. Add render logic

Add the following `else if` statement, with "new" replaced, below the cards to make the sub-page visible when desired:

```r
else if (analysis_mode() == "new") {
  new_page_ui(session$ns("new"))
}
```

### 4. Add navigation logic

Add the following `observeEvent`, with "new" replaced, below the previous step to add the navigation logic:

```r
observeEvent(input$go_new, {
  analysis_mode("new")
})
```

### 5. Back and Next navigation

If the new sub-page has a **Go back** and **Go to Next Step** button, add the following with the correct naming:

```r
observeEvent(new_result$go_back(), {
  analysis_mode("hub")
})

observeEvent(new_result$go_next(), {
  go_next_trigger(Sys.time())
})
```
## Finalizing Additions

After completing the above steps, check that:

- Module IDs match across the UI and Server sections
- The application launches without errors
- Navigation is available and functional, both through the navigation bar and the "Go to" and "Back" buttons
- The correct input and output are transferred between steps
